Hope you're well — SprintPilot is planning a staged national rollout of our new ‘Offers’ feature the week of Nov 7, and we expect a concentrated generation spike during the first 36 hours of the send window. We ran a simulation and expect an intermittent peak of ~1,000 req/s for ~2 hours, with average payload size ~900 tokens. Normal baseline usage will remain below 200 req/s.

As discussed in the PoC, we want to request a temporary carveout for:
- Burst ceiling: increase from our standard 200 req/s to 1,200 req/s for the 36-hour window (primary burst behavior).
- Latency SLO: allowance to relax p95 target from 150ms to 300ms during the burst period if necessary.
- Fairness policy: exemption from fairness-driven throttling for our cached prefixes during the window.

Attached are the send plan and traffic forecast. Can Redwood confirm whether this is feasible and what guardrails you’d require (rate ramp, rollback triggers, costs/credits)? We need to finalize procurement and schedule by EOD Nov 5.

Thanks — Maya

Team — quick assessment and recommended controls below. I’ve attached a short runbook / proposal for a temporary SLO carveout.

Summary assessment:
- Feasibility: Yes, we can support a 36-hour prioritized window with a staged ramp to 1,200 req/s, assuming the following mitigations are applied.
- Risk: Medium. Main risk is transient tail-latency increase for co-tenants and cache eviction effects if KV prefix caching isn’t tuned.

Required guardrails:
1) Ramp profile: 0 -> 400 req/s (10m), 400 -> 800 req/s (20m), 800 -> 1,200 req/s (30m). Auto-abort if error-rate > 3% sustained for 5m or p99 latency > 1s for 3m.
2) Token budget: require SprintPilot to pre-purchase a one-time burst token bucket (billing/contract detail to follow).
3) Fairness: grant a prefix-level exemption for cached prefixes only (not full tenant exemption) and enable automatic rollback to fairness pool if overall cluster load exceeds 70% of capacity.
4) Observability: enable per-route tracing and a live dashboard; Redwood will stream realtime metrics to a read-only dashboard and set alerting channels.

Operational notes:
- We’ll deploy the policy as a temporary routing rule tied to their tenant id + a rolling limit enforcement in the router.
- Post-window: we’ll run a short health sweep (24h) and provide a short incident report.

I’ve attached: redwood-temporary-slo-proposal.pdf (runbook + rollback thresholds). Happy to tighten the conditions; once commercial confirms token purchase and acceptance of rollback triggers we can schedule the change.

—Karthik

Attachments: redwood-temporary-slo-proposal.pdf
